Collapse

Collapse expands and retracts a single content block with a smooth height animation. It is the lowest-level disclosure primitive behind accordions and expandable panels.

Basic Collapse

Point a trigger at its target with data-zak-collapse="#id". The target is .zak-collapse-target; add .zak-collapse-active to start open.

Release 3.2 shipped today. It adds push-mode drawers, a date range picker and faster theme switching. See the changelog for breaking changes.
HTML
<button class="zak-btn zak-btn-primary" data-zak-collapse="#collapseBasic">
    Toggle details
</button>

<div class="zak-collapse-target zak-collapse-active" id="collapseBasic">
    <div class="coll-box">Release 3.2 shipped today...</div>
</div>

Collapse with Icon

Swap the chevron state from the zak:open / zak:close events for a tidy disclosure affordance.

Multiple Collapses

You can drive several targets with one trigger by listing multiple selectors, or use two independent buttons for the same target.

Section A content — filters like status, assignee and priority.
Section B content — sorting and grouping controls.

Horizontal Collapse

For width animation, override the transition to animate width and set height: auto on the target.

This collapses horizontally using width animation.

CSS Classes & Variables

HTML
/* Class Summary */
.zak-collapse-target   /* Collapsible region (height: 0 by default) */
.zak-collapse-active   /* Expanded state (height: auto) */

/* Variables used */
--zak-transition-medium /* Animation duration */
--zak-ease-standard     /* Easing curve */

JavaScript

HTML
// Data attributes (automatic)
//   data-zak-collapse="#id"  toggle the target

// Programmatic API
zak.collapse.open('#myTarget');
zak.collapse.close('#myTarget');
zak.collapse.toggle('#myTarget');

// Events on the target element
target.addEventListener('zak:open', function () {});
target.addEventListener('zak:close', function () {});

// Height is animated, so open is async:
zak.collapse.open('#myTarget').then(function () {
    console.log('fully expanded');
});

Accessibility

  • The trigger is a <button> and toggles aria-expanded automatically.
  • The target gets aria-hidden sync while collapsed so hidden content stays out of the accessibility tree.
  • Use aria-controls so assistive tech can jump from trigger to panel.
  • Never nest bootstrap-style double-tap triggers; one button controls one or more panels with clear labels.
  • Avoid animating display; the height transition keeps layout stable and predictable.
